title: Decode, Meniscus, Trim & Buzz
description: Five patterns riding the platform's edge: JS-free enter/exit transitions, a liquid meniscus nav, optical text-box trimming, real haptics, and a zero-JS carousel.

drops.title: Zero-JS Enter & Exit
drops.description: Cards animate in on insert and out on removal using only native CSS — no animation library.
drops.concept: New elements are matched by an @starting-style override for their first paint, then transition to their normal state. On removal, JS just toggles a class; because `display` is included in the transition with `transition-behavior: allow-discrete`, the browser keeps rendering the old layout for the full transition before swapping to display:none.
drops.source: web-standards.dev, "Entry and Exit Transitions with Modern CSS"

interaction.mouse: Click a card's ✕ to dismiss it, or toggle auto-stream

drops.title: Meniscus Liquid Nav
drops.description: A bottom nav whose surface bends around a spring-driven bead like a real bead of liquid.
drops.concept: The bar's top edge is drawn as an SVG path with a smooth Bezier dip that always re-centers on the bead's live x-position. A single spring integrator drives the bead toward the active tab, and its signed velocity stretches whichever shoulder of the dip is trailing — giving the whole bar a fluid, surface-tension feel with no animation library.

interaction.mouse: Click a tab to send the bead there

drops.title: The End of Magic Padding
drops.description: text-box-trim removes invisible line-box padding so a single uniform value sits optically centered.
drops.concept: Browsers reserve half-leading space above and below every line box, which is why chips/buttons/headlines always need slightly asymmetric padding to look centered. `text-box-trim` (via the `text-box` shorthand with a `text-box-edge` like `cap alphabetic`) trims that space away entirely, so one padding value works across every typeface and size.

interaction.mouse: Change the text-box-edge preset and toggle guides

drops.title: Feel the Interface
drops.description: Real device haptic patterns via navigator.vibrate(), visualized as a synced waveform.
drops.concept: Each interaction intent (tap, success, error, hold) maps to a pulse/pause array passed straight to navigator.vibrate(). Since vibration has no visible signal of its own, a bar-waveform lights up in exact sync with each pulse's duration, making the invisible pattern legible even on devices without a vibration motor.

interaction.mouse: Click a button to trigger its pattern
interaction.touch: Real haptics fire on supported devices

drops.title: A Carousel With No JavaScript
drops.description: Native dot markers and prev/next arrows — zero JavaScript for navigation.
drops.concept: `scroll-marker-group: after` on the scroll container renders a native marker for each `::scroll-marker` child; `:target-current` highlights whichever marker matches the currently snapped slide. `::scroll-button(inline-start/inline-end)` generates real prev/next controls on the container itself — click, tab, and arrow-key navigation all work natively.
drops.source: Jo Mändle, "Native CSS Carousels with ::scroll-button and ::scroll-marker"

interaction.mouse: Click dots or arrows, or drag to scroll
